_why: Written 2026-08-08. Saffra is the FLEET EXCEPTION twice over: it is the only app that requires an account (root site-audit-contract.json already records that), and it is the only app that ships a product-analytics SDK. Both approvals below are therefore narrow, and the evidence exists to stop a future editor 'simplifying' them into the fleet-standard wording, which would be false here. Verified against /Users/dee/Developer/DrVanus/saffra-ios and the masterchef-api Fly secrets.

evidence: The claim on index.html is 'We never track you across apps or websites' — CROSS-APP tracking, which is what Apple's ATT governs. saffra-ios/MasterChef/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares NSPrivacyTracking = false with an EMPTY NSPrivacyTrackingDomains array, and no AppTrackingTransparency / ATTrackingManager / IDFA use appears anywhere in the app.

SAFFRA DOES SHIP ANALYTICS, and the sentence is worded to be true anyway. saffra-ios/MasterChef/Utilities/Telemetry.swift wraps PostHogSDK; Info.plist:54-57 carries MCPostHogAPIKey / MCPostHogHost fed from the MC_POSTHOG_API_KEY build setting, whose default is empty (project.yml:169) and which is injected at build time. Telemetry.start() refuses to initialise unless the key is non-empty AND begins with 'phc_'. It is first-party product analytics, not cross-app tracking.

The wiring is deliberately narrow: captureApplicationLifecycleEvents = false and captureScreenViews = false, so only explicitly-fired events are sent, and a user opt-out is persisted in UserDefaults (DefaultsKey.optOut) and re-applied on cold launch.

The site already discloses it rather than denying it: support.html:127 offers 'Opt out of analytics — stops anonymous usage events', and privacy.html:122 lists 'Any analytics that track you across apps or websites' among the things Saffra does NOT do. DO NOT rewrite any of these to 'no analytics' or 'no tracking' full stop — that would be false while Telemetry.swift ships.

SCOPED TO THIRD-PARTY LOOKUPS ONLY, which is how both pages use it. privacy.html attaches 'No personal data' to the Nutritionix line (ingredient names are sent to look up nutrition information) and support.html attaches it to Nutritionix plus Open Food Facts (just the barcode number). Neither call carries a user identifier.

SAFFRA COLLECTS PERSONAL DATA ELSEWHERE and the site says so: it is the one app in the fleet that requires an account (saffra-ios/MasterChef/App/MasterChefApp.swift:118-125 gates the root view on sign-in), sign-in is Apple AND Google, and chat/vision/Whisper/TTS/embeddings all leave to OpenAI (masterchef-api config.py:20-23; verified 2026-08-08 in SITE-CONTRADICTIONS-RESOLVED-2026-08-08.md §4). A page-level 'we collect no personal data' would be false — keep this phrase attached to the specific outbound lookup it describes.

contract_notes: If MC_POSTHOG_API_KEY is ever baked into a shipping build, re-check the App Privacy answers in App Store Connect and the analytics wording on support.html before release. The gate cannot see a build-time-injected key, so this is a human check.
